nodes.text: Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is infinitely vertex-connected?

#1068 : [Va99,7.90] graph theory | set theory | chromatic number This is described in [BoPi24] as a 'version of the Erdős-Hajnal problem' (which is [1067] ), but it does not seem to appear in [ErHa66] . We say a graph is infinitely (vertex) connected if any two vertices are connected by infinitely many pairwise vertex-disjoint paths. Soukup [So15] constructed a graph with uncountable chromatic number in which every uncountable set is finitely vertex-connected. A simpler construction was given by Bowler and Pitz [BoPi24] . See also [1067] .
